mainTopic: Why the שליח says ״בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם״, how many people must be present when the גט is given, and how much of the writing the שליח must see.
overview: The גמרא continues explaining why a שליח bringing a גט from abroad must say ״בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם״. It shows that the argument of רבה and רבא matches an older dispute: one view says the reason is that people abroad were not experts in writing a גט לשמה, and the other says it is that witnesses are not available to confirm the signatures (קיום). A story proves that רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the לשמה reason, so רבי יוחנן holds קיום. The גמרא then explains why רבי שמעון בר אבא could skip the declaration: a second man was with him. Next, רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא argue whether the גט is handed over in front of two people or three. After rejecting two explanations, the גמרא settles on this: the question is whether we worry that people would rely on a woman שליח as one of the judges. A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן's view of two, and the גמרא explains רבי מאיר's harsh ruling there by his strict rule about the חכמים' set formula for גיטין. Finally, stories with בר הדיא and רבה בר בר חנה show that a שליח does not need to watch every letter. Even one line written לשמה in front of him is enough, and רב אשי's added view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The declaration only protects against the husband's challenge
steps.stepSummary: The reason for the declaration is the fear that the husband will contest the גט. If he is not contesting, the court should not raise the challenge on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for the declaration? Perhaps the husband will come, contest the גט, and make it invalid. But now the husband is not contesting. Should we get up and contest it ourselves?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the logic behind a lenient position. The declaration is only a safeguard against the husband, so when he is not complaining, the court does not need to worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reasoning treats the declaration as protection against a future challenge (ערעור) by the husband. It is not presented as a basic requirement of the גט itself. Since nobody is challenging here, the court has no reason to create a problem that does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Contests or challenges (the validity of the גט)
Invalidates
Now, in this case

steps.confusionAlert: The ending ״אנן ניקום ונערער עלה?!״ is a rhetorical question. It means: we certainly should not challenge it ourselves.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Perhaps the husband will come and contest
and invalidate it;
now that the husband is not contesting,
shall we get up and contest it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מַאי – דִּילְמָא אָתֵי בַּעַל מְעַרְעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind a position discussed just before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration only guards against the husband's challenge. Where the husband does not contest, the court does not contest the גט either.

steps.title: The discussion depends on the dispute of רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the disagreement between רבה and רבא matches the dispute of רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי about why the declaration was required: either because people are not experts in לשמה, or because witnesses are not available to confirm the signatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: This depends on the dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. One said: it is because they are not experts in writing a גט for her sake. The other said: it is because witnesses are not available to confirm it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the discussion to an older, more basic dispute about the reason for the declaration. This sets up the next move: figuring out which אמורא holds which reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is קיום (confirming the signatures), the declaration only protects against the husband's challenge. That fits the reasoning in step 1. If the reason is לשמה, the declaration protects the basic validity of the גט, so it matters even when nobody is contesting. The text says ״חד אמר... וחד אמר״ without telling us who said which, so that has to be worked out.

keyTerms.meaning: In (depending on) the dispute
For her sake: the גט must be written specifically for this woman
Experts, knowledgeable
To confirm it (verify the witnesses' signatures)
One said... and one said (we are not told who said which)

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons lead to different results in practice. The קיום reason only matters if someone challenges the גט. The לשמה reason concerns whether the גט was written properly at all.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: It is a matter of the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
phrases.notes: At the start of the מסכת, רבה and רבא argued about why the agent must say this. Their argument matches this dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: one said: because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ.
phrases.english: and one said: because witnesses are not available to confirm it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the preceding reasoning inside a larger, earlier dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The issue depends on whether the declaration exists because of לשמה or because of קיום.

steps.title: A story to show which view is רבי יהושע בן לוי's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who holds the לשמה reason. It brings a story where רבי שמעון בר אבא asked him whether he needed to make the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us conclude that רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who said: because they are not experts in לשמה. For רבי שמעון בר אבא brought a גט before רבי יהושע בן לוי and asked him: Do I need to say ״It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,״ or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify who said which reason, and opens with a story as proof. This step only sets up the question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 left it unclear which אמורא held which reason. The question asked of רבי יהושע בן לוי gives us a chance to hear his own reasoning in his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be concluded, it can be proven
Brought a גט
Do I need to?
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence

phrases.english: Let it be concluded that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: is the one who said: because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא אַיְיתִי גִּיטָּא
phrases.english: for Rabbi Shimon bar Abba brought a bill of divorce
before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
and said to him: Do I need to say
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence," or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to identify the unnamed speakers from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the לשמה reason.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי שמעון בר אבא bringing a גט to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the declaration was only for earlier generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that the declaration is no longer needed. It was required only in earlier generations, when people were not experts in לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You do not need to. They said this only in the earlier generations, when people were not experts in לשמה. But in the later generations, when they are experts in לשמה, it is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question, and his reason clearly mentions לשמה. This is the heart of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He ties the need for the declaration to whether people know how to write a גט לשמה. Since that knowledge has spread, the requirement has fallen away. This shows that his reason for the declaration is לשמה, not קיום.

keyTerms.meaning: You do not need to
Earlier generations
Later generations

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is what shows which reason רבי יהושע בן לוי holds. The גמרא will soon question it (step 6), because a rule like this does not simply lapse when the concern seems gone.

phrases.english: He said to him: You do not need to,
they said it only in the earlier generations,
when they were not experts in writing it for her sake,
but in the later generations, when they are experts in writing it for her sake –
no, it is not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the answer that completes the proof begun in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the לשמה reason.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His own words: the declaration was needed only when people were not experts in לשמה.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the לשמה reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who gives the לשמה reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be concluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof and accepts it. רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the לשמה reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the לשמה reason, it follows that רבי יוחנן holds the reason that witnesses are not available to confirm the גט (קיום).
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for ״בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם״: לשמה (רבי יהושע בן לוי) and קיום (רבי יוחנן). The reasoning that we need not worry if the husband does not contest fits the קיום reason.

phrases.english: Let it be concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that the declaration exists because people were not experts in לשמה, so רבי יוחנן holds the קיום reason.

steps.title: How could the agent skip the declaration?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the שליח no longer needs to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. רבה also holds the witnesses reason, and we already said we worry the matter could return to its old broken state.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really accept that? But רבה also holds the reason of רבא! And besides, we said we worry that the matter might return to its corrupt state!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the story of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who told רבי שמעון בר אבא that he did not need to make the declaration. It gives two reasons why the declaration should still be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if people are now experts in לשמה, the other reason is still there: witnesses may not be available to confirm the signatures. On top of that, the גמרא already said the declaration stays even after people became experts, in case things slip back to the old problem. So the shortcut in the story seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? A challenging opener
He holds of / agrees with
Lest the matter go back to its broken state
And furthermore, a second challenge

phrases.english: And can you really understand this?!
phrases.notes: He is questioning the idea that the שליח could skip saying בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

phrases.english: But רבה holds the reason of רבא too!
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא showed that רבה also accepts רבא's reason, that witnesses may not be available.

phrases.english: And furthermore, we already said
that we worry the matter will return to its corrupt state!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא?! וְהָא רַבָּה אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story used as proof in steps 3-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in the story that the שליח no longer needs to make the declaration.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The witnesses reason still applies. Also, a rule of חכמים does not lapse, because we fear the old problem will return.

steps.title: There was a second man with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר אבא had another person with him, so there were two witnesses. The story left that person out to protect רבי שמעון's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון בר אבא had another man with him. The reason the story does not count him is out of respect for רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The declaration was not needed in this case because two people were bringing the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two people bring the גט, they can serve as witnesses themselves. So the worry about confirming the signatures does not apply, and the rule was never meant for this case. The other man is not mentioned only out of respect for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person
With him
Did not count or mention him
His honor

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the declaration is never needed today. The shortcut worked only because there were two people, and that is the reason the story could skip it.

phrases.english: Rather, רבי שמעון בר אבא
had another person with him,
phrases.notes: With two of them, they count as two witnesses, so the declaration is not needed.

phrases.english: and the reason the story does not mention him
is because of the honor of רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא אִינִישׁ אַחֲרִינָא הֲוָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by explaining the facts of the story differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: two people brought the גט, not one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בר אבא brought the גט alone, so skipping the declaration would break the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had a second person with him, so they served as two witnesses and no declaration was needed.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of saying בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם stays in place. In the story it was skipped only because two people brought the גט.

steps.title: In front of how many people is the גט given?
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא argue whether the שליח gives the גט in front of two people or three, but we do not yet know who holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: In front of how many does he give it to her? רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא disagree. One says in front of two, and one says in front of three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how many people must be there when the שליח hands the גט to the woman. It sets up the next step, which will try to figure out who said what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that people must be present. The only question is whether two are enough or three are needed. The names are not attached to the opinions yet.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, introducing a dispute of אמוראים
In front of how many
He gives it to her
One said, without saying which one

phrases.english: It was stated:
In front of how many people does he give it to her?
phrases.notes: "He" is the שליח bringing the גט from overseas.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא disagree;
one says: in front of two,
and one says: in front of three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether the גט is given in front of two or three people. Which אמורא holds which view is not yet known.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יוחנן says two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story: רבי יוחנן told רבין בר רב חסדא to give the גט in front of two people and make the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us conclude that רבי יוחנן is the one who says two. רבין בר רב חסדא brought a גט before רבי יוחנן, and he told him: Go give it to her in front of two, and tell them, 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out which side of the מחלוקת belongs to רבי יוחנן. It brings a real case he ruled on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, רבי יוחנן said two people are enough. So he must be the one who holds 'two,' and רבי חנינא must hold 'three.'

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be concluded, proposing to settle who holds what
Go give it to her
In front of two
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence

phrases.english: Let us conclude that רבי יוחנן
is the one who said in front of two,
for רבין בר רב חסדא
brought a גט before רבי יוחנן,
and he said to him: Go, give it to her
in front of two,
and say to them
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to assign the two opinions of step 8 to the right אמוראים.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds the גט is given in front of two people.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case: רבי יוחנן told רבין בר רב חסדא to give the גט in front of two.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: רבי יוחנן is the one who says two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is concluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the story as proof. רבי יוחנן holds 'two,' so רבי חנינא holds 'three.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one challenges the proof, so the names are now attached to the opinions. The גט is given in front of two people according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the שליח gives the גט in front of two people and says בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. רבי חנינא says three.

phrases.english: It is concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof of step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן holds that the גט is given in front of two, and רבי חנינא holds three.

steps.title: Suggestion: the two-or-three argument depends on the reason for the declaration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that whoever says two holds the reason is לשמה, and whoever says three holds the reason is קיום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is what they argue about. The one who says 'in front of two' holds the reason is that people are not experts in writing a גט לשמה. The one who says 'in front of three' holds the reason is that witnesses are not around to confirm the גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא. It links their argument to the two reasons for the declaration that we learned earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is לשמה, the שליח is just testifying how it was written, and two witnesses are enough. If the reason is קיום, he is confirming a document, and confirming a document needs a בית דין of three. So each number would match one reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. The גמרא offers a suggestion, often one it will later reject.
They argue about
Experts in writing the גט for her sake, meaning for this specific woman
Witnesses who are around to confirm the signatures on the document

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion. The גמרא is about to reject it, so do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: Let us say that they argue about this:
that the one who says 'in front of two'
holds: because they are not experts in writing it for her sake;
phrases.notes: This is the reason given earlier in the סוגיא, by רבה and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: and the one who says 'in front of three'

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ?
phrases.english: holds: because there are no witnesses around to confirm it?
phrases.notes: This is רבא's reason from earlier. Confirming a document needs three people, like a בית דין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know רבי יוחנן says two, the גמרא tries to explain the reason behind the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: two people means the reason is לשמה; three people means the reason is קיום.

steps.title: First rejection: רבי יוחנן holds the קיום reason, yet he says two
steps.stepSummary: Earlier we proved that רבי יוחנן holds the reason is קיום. Under the suggestion, he should then require three, but he says two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? We know that רבי יהושע בן לוי said the reason is לשמה, so רבי יוחנן must be the one who said the reason is קיום. So how can רבי יוחנן say 'in front of two' here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion by pointing to what we already know about רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that רבי יוחנן argues with רבי יהושע בן לוי, so רבי יוחנן holds the קיום reason. Under the suggestion, קיום means three people. But Step 10 proved that רבי יוחנן says two, so the suggestion does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you think so? This opens a strong rejection.
The אמורא who holds the reason is לשמה
How?

phrases.english: And can you really think so?!

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר
phrases.english: But since רבי יהושע בן לוי said
'because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,'
רבי יוחנן must be the one who said
'because there are no witnesses around to confirm it,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא הֵיכִי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם?
phrases.english: so here, how can רבי יוחנן say 'in front of two'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that two goes with לשמה and three goes with קיום
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן holds the קיום reason but says two, which goes against the suggestion.

steps.title: Second rejection: even the לשמה view also needs קיום
steps.stepSummary: רבה, who gives the לשמה reason, also agrees with רבא's קיום reason. So no one holds only the לשמה reason, and the suggestion falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רבה also holds רבא's reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem with the suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 6) we saw that רבה also holds the witnesses reason. So even the side that stresses לשמה still needs קיום, which needs three people. The suggested split between the two reasons does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. A second objection follows.
He holds, he agrees with

phrases.english: And furthermore,
רבה also holds רבא's reason!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא רַבָּה אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that one side relies only on the לשמה reason
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone, even רבה, needs קיום, so the number of people cannot depend on the reason.

steps.title: The real argument: can the agent be a witness and then a judge?
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees we need קיום, which needs a בית דין of three. They argue about whether the שליח, who acts as a witness, can also count as one of the judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that we need the reason of confirming the גט. Here they argue about whether an agent can become a witness and whether a witness can become a judge. The one who says two holds that an agent can become a witness, and a witness can become a judge. The one who says three holds that an agent can become a witness, but a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the מחלוקת. Both sides hold the קיום reason, but they argue about the role of the שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Confirming a document needs a בית דין of three. If the שליח, who testifies, can also be a judge, he plus two others make three, so two people are enough. If a witness cannot be a judge, the שליח does not count, so three other people are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings in a new explanation in place of the rejected one.
Everyone agrees
An agent can become a witness about his own mission
A witness can become a judge in the same matter

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides need קיום, which needs three judges. Two people are enough only if the שליח himself can be both a witness and a judge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the מחלוקת away from the reason for the תקנה: both sides need קיום. The idea that it depends on a witness serving as a judge is challenged in step 15 and replaced in step 16.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees that we need
the reason of witnesses being around to confirm it,
and here they argue about whether an agent can become a witness
and whether a witness can become a judge:
The one who says 'in front of two'
holds: an agent can become a witness,
and a witness can become a judge.
phrases.notes: So the שליח joins the two others, and together they make a בית דין of three.

phrases.english: And the one who says 'in front of three'
holds: an agent can become a witness,
but a witness cannot become a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בָּעֵינַן עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both rejections, the גמרא offers a new explanation of the מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the argument: from which reason applies to whether a witness can serve as a judge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument about two or three depended on the reason for the declaration.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides hold the קיום reason. They argue only about whether the שליח-witness can also count as a judge.

steps.title: But a witness can become a judge in rabbinic matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer, since we already hold that in דרבנן matters an עד can become a דיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we hold that in rabbinic matters a witness can become a judge?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 14, which said the argument is about whether the שליח, who acts like a witness, can count as a judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Confirming a document (קיום) here is only a rabbinic requirement. We already have a set rule that in דרבנן matters an עד נעשה דיין. So there should be no argument: the שליח can surely count as one of the three judges.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us
A law from the Rabbis, not from the Torah
A witness can become a judge in the same case

phrases.english: But don't we hold
that in rabbinic matters a witness can become a judge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14 using an established rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 14 that the two views argue about whether the שליח-witness can count as a judge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an accepted rule that in דרבנן matters an עד נעשה דיין, so that cannot be the point they argue about.

steps.title: They argue about a woman bringing the גט
steps.stepSummary: New explanation: the view requiring three worries that a woman might bring the גט and people would rely on her, but she cannot be a judge. רבי יוחנן says people know a woman cannot be a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here this is what they argue about. One master holds: since a woman is also fit to bring the גט, sometimes a woman will bring it and they will rely on her. The other holds: about a woman, people know, and they will not rely on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier answer and gives a new reason for the argument: whether we worry about a case where a woman is the שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the שליח can usually count as the third judge. But a woman may also bring a גט, and she cannot be a judge. The view that needs three is afraid people would rely on her as if she were the third, leaving only two, so it always requires three. רבי יוחנן says everyone knows a woman cannot be a judge, so they would bring a third person anyway, and no extra rule is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
They argue
Fit to be the שליח who brings the גט
They rely on her
They surely know

steps.confusionAlert: Rely on her does not mean trusting her report. It means treating her as if she counts as one of the three judges, which she cannot.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: everyone needs קיום with three, and everyone agrees the male שליח can count. The argument is only whether we make a rule of three because of a woman שליח.

phrases.english: Rather, here they argue about this:
One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is the view that requires three people.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁירָה לְהָבִיא אֶת הַגֵּט,
phrases.english: since a woman is fit to bring the bill of divorce,
sometimes a woman will bring it
and they will rely on her.
phrases.notes: They would count her as the third judge, even though a woman can't be one.

phrases.english: And the other holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן, who says two are enough.

phrases.english: a woman – they surely know
and they will not rely on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by replacing the step 14 explanation with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of disagreement (from whether a witness can judge, to whether we worry about a woman שליח).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was whether the שליח can count as a judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree he can count. The argument is whether we require three in every case because a woman שליח cannot count.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in line with רבי יוחנן. It starts with רבי מאיר's ruling about a שליח who gave the גט without saying בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא like רבי יוחנן: One who brings a גט from overseas and gave it to her but did not say to her, 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' her second husband must divorce her and the child is a ממזר. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. Here we only hear the first opinion, from רבי מאיר, and the proof itself will come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is very strict: if the שליח did not make the statement, the woman is not divorced at all. If she remarries, she must leave her second husband and the child is a ממזר. The part that actually supports רבי יוחנן comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view
A country overseas
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence
He must divorce her (the second husband)
A child from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the general community

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in accordance with רבי יוחנן:
One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,
and gave it to her
but did not say to her:
'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence' –
he must divorce her, and the child is a mamzer,
phrases.notes: He means her second husband, if she remarried relying on this גט.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the argument, the גמרא opens a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's view that two are enough.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the שליח needs to make his statement before only two others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, starting with רבי מאיר's strict ruling. The supporting part comes in step 18.

steps.title: The חכמים' view and the fix: give the גט again in front of two
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The חכמים say the child is not a ממזר. To fix things, the שליח takes the גט back and gives it again in front of two people while saying בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: the child is not a ממזר. What should he do? He should take the גט back from her, give it to her again in front of two people, and say: 'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it brought to support רבי יוחנן. The key detail is that the fix needs only two people, not three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is mostly about whether the child is a ממזר. Along the way it says the גט is given again 'in front of two.' If three judges were truly needed, the ברייתא would have said three. So it fits the view that two are enough and that there is no worry about people relying on a woman, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden relationship, such as from a married woman with another man
How should he act? (What is the fix?)
In front of two people
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence: the declaration a שליח makes when delivering a גט from abroad

steps.whyThisMatters: This detail of 'two, not three' is the actual proof the גמרא was looking for when it brought this ברייתא.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
The child is not a mamzer.
How should he act?
phrases.notes: "He" is the שליח who forgot to say the words. The ברייתא now gives the fix.

phrases.english: He should take it from her,
and give it to her again in front of two,
and say: 'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 17 and supplies the actual proof point.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's position that two are enough and there is no worry that people will rely on a woman as a judge
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's fix: the גט is given again 'in front of two'

steps.title: Is רבי מאיר really that strict over missing words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. Would רבי מאיר really break up the second marriage and call the child a ממזר just because the שליח did not say the declaration?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר holds that just because he did not say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' the second husband must divorce her and the child is a ממזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns back to רבי מאיר's ruling from the start of the ברייתא and questions how harsh it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שליח may really have seen the גט written and signed. He only failed to say so. Calling the child a ממזר over a missing sentence seems far too strict, so the גמרא asks how רבי מאיר could rule this way.

keyTerms.meaning: He must send her out: the second husband must divorce her
The child
Because he did not say

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
because he did not say
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,'
he must divorce her, and the child is a mamzer?
phrases.notes: "He must divorce" means the man she married afterward has to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי מאיר's ruling in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that she must leave her second husband and the child is a ממזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving out a spoken declaration seems too small a mistake to make the גט invalid and the child a ממזר.

steps.title: Yes: רבי מאיר holds that changing the חכמים' formula ruins a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. רבי מאיר is being consistent: he holds that anyone who changes the set formula the חכמים made for גיטין causes the second marriage to be broken up, and the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning. For רב המנונא said in the name of עולא: רבי מאיר used to say, anyone who changes the formula the חכמים set for גיטין, the second husband must divorce her and the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that רבי מאיר has a general rule. This case is just one example of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the declaration is part of the official form the חכמים set. Changing that form is serious, even if the facts behind it were true. So his harsh ruling here is not strange; it follows his steady approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Follows his own reasoning (consistent with his other rulings)
In the name of
One who changes or deviates
The set formula the Sages established, literally 'the coin the Sages minted'

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר is very strict about the set form of גיטין. Any change from the חכמים' formula means she must leave her second husband and the child is a ממזר.

phrases.english: Yes, Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning.
For Rav Hamnuna said in the name of Ulla:
Rabbi Meir would say:
Anyone who changes
from the formula that the Sages set for bills of divorce –
phrases.notes: Literally "the coin the Sages minted." It means a fixed form, stamped once and for all, like a coin.

phrases.english: he must divorce her, and the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the surprise of step 19 by showing that רבי מאיר is consistent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and grounds it in a general rule of the same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's ruling seemed far too harsh for a missing sentence.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds as a general rule that changing the חכמים' formula for גיטין invalidates the second marriage, so this ruling fits.

steps.title: בר הדיא is told to watch every single letter
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. בר הדיא wanted to bring a גט and asked רבי אחי, who was in charge of גיטין. רבי אחי told him he must stand over every single letter as it is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הדיא wanted to bring a גט. He came before רבי אחי, who was appointed over גיטין. רבי אחי said to him: You must stand over each and every letter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a story. It asks how closely a שליח who will say בפני נכתב must watch the writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחי holds the strict view. To truly say 'it was written in my presence,' the שליח must watch every letter being written. This sets up the disagreement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring a גט (as a שליח)
Appointed, put in charge
To stand over, to watch closely
Each and every letter

phrases.english: Bar Hedya wanted to bring a bill of divorce,
he came before Rabbi Achai,
who was appointed over bills of divorce,
he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ אַתָּה לַעֲמוֹד עַל כָּל אוֹת וָאוֹת.
phrases.english: You need to stand over each and every letter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how much the שליח must actually see before he can say בפני נכתב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אחי, a שליח must watch every letter of the גט being written.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי say it is not needed
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא then asked רבי אמי and רבי אסי. They told him he does not need to watch every letter.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי אמי and רבי אסי. They said to him: You do not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: בר הדיא asks other חכמים, and they disagree with רבי אחי's strict demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי and רבי אסי hold that the שליח does not have to stand over each letter. In general being there and overseeing the writing is enough for him to say 'in my presence.' Now there are two opposing opinions on how closely he must watch.

keyTerms.meaning: He came before (to ask a ruling)
They said to him
You do not need to

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
they said to him: You do not need to.
phrases.notes: He means he does not need to watch each letter. Being there and overseeing in general is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing ruling to רבי אחי's strict demand in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אמי and רבי אסי, the שליח does not need to watch every letter of the גט being written.

steps.title: Being extra strict would cast doubt on earlier גיטין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי explain why one should not choose to be strict and watch every letter: doing so would suggest that all earlier גיטין were not done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, 'I will just be strict and watch every letter anyway,' then you are casting doubt on all the earlier גיטין, whose שליחים never did this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the words of רבי אמי and רבי אסי. They reject the idea of being strict just to be safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think: why not follow רבי אחי just to be extra careful? The answer is that being strict here is not harmless. If watching every letter were truly needed, then all the גיטין brought in earlier times, where the שליח did not do this, would look invalid. That would cast doubt on those divorces and on the children of the second marriages.

keyTerms.meaning: To be strict, to choose the stricter path
Casting a bad name or doubt on something
The earlier gittin, the ones given in past times

steps.confusionAlert: Usually being strict sounds safe. Here the גמרא teaches that a needless חומרא can actually cause harm, because it suggests earlier גיטין were not valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the halacha does not require the שליח to watch every letter. Extra strictness here would damage the standing of many past divorces.

phrases.english: And if you would say: I will act stringently,
it turns out that you are casting aspersions
on the earlier bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי from step 22 by blocking the option of following רבי אחי out of caution.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea of following רבי אחי's strict rule just to be on the safe side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being strict would suggest that earlier גיטין, made without watching every letter, were invalid, casting doubt on them.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה's half-witnessed גט and רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה brought a גט that was only half written in front of him. רבי אלעזר ruled that even if only one line was written לשמה in front of the שליח, he does not need to see more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה brought a גט. Half of it was written in front of him, and half was not. He came to ask רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר told him: even if the scribe wrote only one line of it for her sake in front of you, you do not need anything more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about how much of the writing a שליח must see. רבי אלעזר gives a very lenient answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה was unsure whether he could say בפני נכתב when he saw only half the writing. רבי אלעזר said that seeing even one line written לשמה is enough. Once we see the scribe writing for this woman, we assume the whole גט was written for her. This fits with רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who also said the שליח does not need to watch every letter.

keyTerms.meaning: Half
Was written in front of him
One line of writing
For her sake: written for this specific woman
He no longer needs anything more

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a very low minimum. The שליח only needs to see a small part of the writing done לשמה to be able to say בפני נכתב.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אַיְיתִי גִּיטָּא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana brought a bill of divorce,
half of it was written in his presence
and half of it was not written in his presence.
He came before Rabbi Elazar,
He said to him:
Even if the scribe wrote in it
only one line for her sake,
he no longer needs anything more.
phrases.notes: He does not need to see the rest of the writing; we assume all of it was done for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אַיְיתִי גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story on the same question of how much writing the שליח must see, giving an even more lenient measure than steps 22-23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if the שליח saw only one line written לשמה, he can say בפני נכתב and does not need to see more.

steps.title: רב אשי begins his view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב אשי, who is about to give his own opinion on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is opening the next statement, from רב אשי, which continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After רבי אלעזר's lenient measure of one line, the גמרא brings another אמורא. רב אשי's words come next, and they will add his view on how much of the writing the שליח must see.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading later אמורא in Bavel

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a new opinion following רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רב אשי's statement, which continues in the next section.
